summary.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 2.4% YoY to INR 1,094.21 crore, but PBT fell to INR 202.49 crore from INR 249.54 crore and PAT to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore. Management cited EBITDA margin around 24% and PAT margin around 14% for the quarter. The company delivered three vessels in the period, plus three by subsidiary Udupi Cochin Shipyard. Management announced several strategic moves: a 50:50 JV with Drydocks World for the ISRF ship repair facility, a scaled-down block fabrication plan after HD KSOE talks failed, a Tuticorin hybrid yard lease, and a Green Maritime battery JV.

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Management said shipbuilding is about 70% of turnover at 10-12% EBITDA margin. Deliveries in FY27 so far include the third of eight ASW shallow water crafts, a second multipurpose vessel for a German client, and a Ro-Ro ferry for Kochi Municipal Corporation.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Ship repair is about 30% of turnover at roughly 20-24% EBITDA margin. ISRF has a 6,000-ton ship lift, about 1,400 m berthing and annual capacity of up to 82 ships.

segments.name: Udupi Cochin Shipyard (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Delivered three vessels in the period: two 3,800 TDW general cargo vessels to Wilson Group, Norway, and a 70-tonne bollard pull tug to Polestar Maritime (Adani Group). Management said land constraints limit its new order intake.

segments.name: Green Maritime battery JV (with HBL, 40% CSL)
segments.commentary: Incorporated June 2026 for marinized energy storage systems. Target revenue INR 640 crore by year 5 and about 20% EBITDA margin (ballpark, business plan not final). Total capital INR 50 crore; no manufacturing facility, as HBL will manufacture.

guidance_outlook: Turnover growth guidance of about 12% per year, with management saying it could reach 12-15%.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at around 14-15% for the year on a conservative basis, down from prior years' higher margins.

Target to deliver about 10 vessels in FY27 (three delivered so far in Q1): two more ASWs by December 2026, two more multipurpose vessels, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, and commissioning service vessels and Samskip container vessels through early 2027.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27 as delivery-linked milestone payments come in.
ISRF JV transaction targeted for completion before end of FY27, subject to Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, DIPAM, and CSL shareholder (postal ballot) approvals.
New investments targeted at a return on capital of about 14-15%.
capex_capacity: ISRF JV: INR 1,800 crore slump-sale consideration, 50% in cash and 50% in JV equity. Expected revenue about INR 600 crore over the next 2 years, scaling to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Plan adds 10 workstations.

Block fabrication: Earlier 1 lakh tonne plan with HD KSOE is now a solo facility of about 60,000 tonnes per annum. Current capacity is about 12,000 tonnes per annum, for total throughput near 72,000 tonnes.

Vadinar (Gujarat) ship repair with Deendayal Port Authority: two floating drydocks for ~250 m vessels. CCEA approval received May 2026. Environmental clearance expected shortly; operations targeted within 36 months of EC. Revenue about INR 300-600 crore after 3 years.

Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar Port): won 30-year lease at one-time payment of INR 305.76 crore for about 110 acres land and 17.29 acres waterfront. In DPR stage; revenue of INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years.

Total capex over about 5 years estimated by an analyst at INR 6,000-6,500 crore across the four projects. Funding targeted at about 80:20 debt-equity. Applied for Shipbuilding Development Scheme (25% capex subsidy) and MDF Interest Incentivisation Fund (up to 3% interest subvention).
demand_pricing: Defence pipeline per management: LPD (4 numbers, about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV (12 numbers, about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo (7 numbers, about INR 49,000 crore). Management said these are RFPs with competition; LPD and MCMV seen as more suitable than P-17 Bravo.
NGSV: CSL is L1 for five next-generation survey vessels worth about INR 5,000 crore; order signing expected around November 2026. Navy procedures are slow (CCS and PNC approvals).

Commercial: Dredging Corporation of India sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination basis) expected within about two months. Andaman 4 x 500-passenger vessels under nomination discussion. Government demand aggregation for about 432 vessels over 10 years, with SCI/BCSL tenders in progress. MR tanker technical bid indicative cost about INR 1,700 crore; Aframax EOI indicative cost about INR 2,600 crore.
Export: European commercial vessels from 2023-24 orders are 80-90% complete but only about 30% paid; payment is tail-ended (around 70% on delivery).
Management said the Green Tug Transition Program could create about INR 1,000 crore of battery-led investment over 10 years, with real volume expected in 3-4 years.
